conventions.convention: Channel sequences start at n=1, may have different measurable spaces at different blocklengths, and require no consistency across blocklengths.
A finite DMC has fixed finite nonempty alphabets and block law Wⁿ(yⁿ|xⁿ)=∏ᵢW(yᵢ|xᵢ); the ordinary model imposes neither feedback nor input cost.
Ordinary fixed-length encoders and decoders are deterministic maps, with n,M≥1; encoder injectivity is not required.
Average error averages per-message errors under a uniform message; maximal error is their maximum.
Information density equals ln(W(y|x)/Q(y)) on positive induced joint support and is −∞ elsewhere; block density is its coordinate sum.

Achievability requires codes for every sufficiently large integer blocklength, liminf normalized log message count at least R, and vanishing specified error. Rates are nonnegative and measured in nats per use.
Binary entropy uses natural logarithms and 0 ln 0=0; BSC crossover and BEC erasure parameters include both endpoints.

load_bearing.statement: For every finite DMC W with no input-cost constraint, C_av(W)=C_max(W)=C(W)=max over P_X of I(P_X;W), with rates and mutual information measured in nats per channel use.
For every finite DMC W, the supremum C(W) is a maximum: there is an input probability vector P_X* such that I(P_X*;W)=C(W).
For every input probability vector on Xⁿ and output Yⁿ generated by a finite DMC Wⁿ, one has I(Xⁿ;Yⁿ)≤nC(W).
For every finite DMC W and every 0≤R<C(W), there are fixed-length codes with liminf normalized log message count at least R and average error tending to zero.
Let P_X* attain C(W) and let Q*=P_X*W. If W(y|x)>0, then Q*(y)>0, and for every x∈X, D(W(·|x)||Q*)≤C(W).
Every length-n code with average error ε_av has a subcode with at least M/2 messages and maximal error at most 2ε_av.
Fix a finite DMC W and input law P_X. If (X_i,Y_i) for i≥1 are IID with law P_X(x)W(y|x), then normalized block information density converges in probability to I(P_X;W).

Let P_X* attain C(W) and Q*=P_X*W. There is a finite V≥0 such that for every n≥1, every input word xⁿ, and every δ>0, the Wⁿ(·|xⁿ) probability that ln(Wⁿ(Yⁿ|xⁿ)/(Q*)ⁿ(Yⁿ))>n(C(W)+δ) is at most V/(nδ²). The ratio is evaluated only on the row support.

published_dependencies.used_for: The general channel-sequence definition uses its pointwise probability-kernel requirements.
Positive-domain natural logarithms in information density, divergence, and rates.
Finite entropy, directional KL, and zero-coordinate conventions in attainment, row divergence, and the binary examples.
Continuity of −t ln t at zero in the capacity-attainment proof.
A continuous objective attains its maximum on the nonempty closed bounded input simplex.
Differentiating positive entropy coordinates in the capacity-achieving output-divergence argument.
The product-rule derivative of −t ln t used in the output-divergence argument.
Logarithm identities and monotonicity, including logarithmic divergence at zero in the support argument.

alerts.finding: The page frontmatter contains "status: draft\nitems:" and has no requires field. This omits the task's named prerequisite edge to discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity. Its listed lossless and lossy separation theorems explicitly cite thm-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity-formula and lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-n-letter-information-bound. The mathematical citations are faithful, but the page prerequisite metadata does not record this dependency.

seams_checked.note: The actual imported probability-vector, row-stochastic-kernel, and directional KL definitions agree on finite nonempty alphabets, retained zero coordinates, and natural logarithms. The DMC page does not import a stronger Rényi or testing proposition.

Cost and feedback restrictions are defined separately. Cost-constrained achievability uses the fixed-input IID density lemma within its finite-DMC scope; the inactive-cost corollary invokes the ordinary capacity formula only when every input and code is feasible. Gaussian and feedback claims are not attributed to the ordinary DMC theorem.

Both separation proofs use maximal-error capacity for potentially nonuniform source indices and the n-letter bound for arbitrary input laws. Restricting channel codes preserves retained correct-decoding events. Nats and the all-sufficiently-large-blocklength convention match. The missing page requires field is reported separately in alerts.

The wiretap definition uses finite DMCs for its marginal channels and defines stochastic encoders and secrecy metrics separately. The local density and soft-covering lemmas use finite product channel laws; their additional exponential-tail and secrecy conclusions are proved locally rather than attributed to the ordinary capacity theorem.
